chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) accepted in debt cases the testimony of one man along with the oath of the claimant.'
ai.seo_question: What evidence is required to prove a debt claim in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the flexibility of Shia evidentiary standards by validating a single witness paired with the claimant's oath (*yamin al-mudda'i*) for debt disputes, a ruling distinct from the general requirement of two witnesses. It reflects the practical jurisprudence of Imam Ali (AS), emphasizing ease in commercial transactions while maintaining judicial integrity through the solemnity of the oath. This mechanism serves as a foundational precedent for resolving cases where full corroboration is unavailable but credibility is established.
